get.description:
Returns connected accounts. Only includes accounts within the plan limit by default. Follower data requires analytics add-on.

### Pagination

Server-side pagination is optional. When omitted, returns all accounts (backward-compatible).

- Cursor paging: send `limit` alone for the first page, then pass `pagination.nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is null. Pages are ordered by account id, so accounts added or removed between calls never shift a page. Cannot be combined with `page`, `sort` or `perProfile`.
- Offset paging: send `page` and `limit` together. Out-of-range page/limit values are rejected with 400 rather than silently clamped.

parameters.name: profileId
parameters.description: Filter accounts by profile ID. Must be a valid ObjectId.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Filter accounts by platform (e.g. "instagram", "twitter").

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter accounts by connection status. `connected` returns healthy accounts; `disconnected` returns accounts that need reconnection (per the same reconnection check surfaced in the dashboard). Omit to return accounts in any status. When combined with page/limit, pagination totals reflect the filtered result set.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on the account username, display name or platform user id, or an exact account id. Combine with page/limit to paginate the matches.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Only accounts of this kind. ads = ad accounts (Meta, Google, LinkedIn, Pinterest, TikTok, X, OpenAI, Reddit), communication = WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack and iMessage, blogs = Shopify and WordPress, crm = HubSpot, analytics = Google Analytics, social = every other platform.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort an offset-paginated listing (page and limit) by account name, platform, profile name, status (accounts needing a reconnect first when ascending) or connection date. Ties keep the default order: platform, then newest first.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Direction for `sort`.

parameters.name: includeOverLimit
parameters.description: When true, includes accounts from over-limit profiles.

parameters.name: excludeHidden
parameters.description:
When true, leaves out accounts the dashboard does not show as connections:

- posting accounts with `enabled: false` (ads accounts are always kept, whatever their `enabled` value);
- the internal `sms` and `phone` accounts behind each phone number.

Applied before pagination, so page totals and `statusCounts` count only the remaining accounts. Sandbox accounts added by `includeSandbox` are appended after this filter. Accepts `true` or `false` in any letter case; any other value returns 400.

parameters.name: adAccountRows
parameters.description:
When true, lists every ads account row, one per ad account. By default an API key or OAuth app sees each ads login once per profile and platform, as the single ads connection it had before rows per ad account: its oldest row.

Only changes the result once ads are connected as one row per ad account; until then the two shapes are the same. Applied before pagination. Accepts `true` or `false` in any letter case; any other value returns 400.

parameters.name: includeCreatorAccounts
parameters.description:
When true, also lists the accounts creators connected to your creator campaigns. They sit on creator profiles, which `GET /v1/profiles` does not list, and are left out by default.

Asking for one creator profile by `profileId` lists its accounts either way. Applied before pagination. Accepts `true` or `false` in any letter case; any other value returns 400.

parameters.name: includeSandbox
parameters.description:
When true, appends the shared WhatsApp sandbox account and the iMessage sandbox account to the list when they are active, honouring `platform` but no other filter.

Ignored on a paginated request (page, limit or cursor) and together with `perProfile`. Accepts `true` or `false` in any letter case; any other value returns 400.

parameters.name: includeStatusCounts
parameters.description:
When true, the response carries `statusCounts`: how many accounts match every other
filter of the request (with `status` lifted) in total and how many of those need a
reconnection. Accepts `true` or `false` in any letter case; any other value returns 400.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based) for offset paging. Requires limit; omit page, limit and cursor for all accounts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. With page, an offset page; alone or with cursor, a cursor page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `pagination.nextCursor`; returns the next page of `limit` accounts (500 when limit is omitted). A cursor we cannot parse returns 400. Cannot be combined with page.

parameters.name: profileIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated profile IDs (up to 50) to preview, together with perProfile. The response then also carries `profileTotals`.

parameters.name: perProfile
parameters.description: Return a preview of each profile in profileIds: the newest account of every platform it has, topped up to at least N. Requires profileIds; cannot be combined with page, limit or cursor.

get.description:
Returns all Facebook Pages the connected account has access to, including the currently selected Page and the Instagram professional account linked to each Page.

Works on `facebook` accounts and on `metaads` accounts (classic and Facebook Login for Business connections).

- Business-login `metaads` connection: `selectedPageId` is the default Page ads run as, and every listed Page can be passed as `pageId` on POST /v1/ads/create.
- Classic `metaads` connection: there is no default Page, so `selectedPageId` is null.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: When true, bypasses the page cache and fetches fresh pages from Meta. Rate-limited server-side to 1 refresh per 60s. Pages no longer accessible to the connected account will be removed from the list on refresh.

instagramAccount.description: The Instagram professional account linked to the Page (Meta instagram_business_account), or null when none is linked or the list was served from a cache stored before this field existed (pass refresh=true to re-read it).

id.description: Instagram professional account id, usable as instagramAccountId on POST /v1/ads/create

cached.description: false when this response was just read from Meta (cold cache or a refresh that ran), true when served from the stored list (including a debounced refresh or an empty Meta answer)

404.description: Account not found, or not a facebook or metaads account

get.description:
Returns the account's remaining content-publishing quota for Instagram's rolling
24-hour window, so you can pace publishing and warn before the cap is reached.

`quotaUsage` counts containers published since the start of the window.
Always compare against the returned `quotaTotal` rather than hardcoding a number:
Meta's prose documentation and the live API disagree on the value, and the live
value is authoritative.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The ID of the Instagram account

200.description: Remaining publishing quota for the rolling window

quotaUsage.description: Containers published so far in the current window

quotaDurationSeconds.description: Length of the rolling window in seconds

post.description: Get a presigned URL to upload files directly to cloud storage (up to 5GB). Returns an uploadUrl and publicUrl. PUT your file to the uploadUrl, then use the publicUrl in your posts.

filename.description: Name of the file to upload

size.description: Optional file size in bytes for pre-validation (max 5GB)

uploadUrl.description: Presigned URL to PUT your file to (expires in 1 hour)

publicUrl.description: Public URL where the file will be accessible after upload

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the presigned uploadUrl expires (always 3600)

400.description: Invalid request (missing filename, unsupported contentType, or size out of range)

post.description:
Create a post, and optionally publish it in the same request. A post published immediately (`publishNow: true`) comes back with `platformPostUrl` in the response.

`content` is optional in four cases:

- media is attached
- all platforms have `customContent`
- every platform entry is an X Article (`platformSpecificData.article`)
- every platform entry is a LinkedIn text-free reshare (`platformSpecificData.reshareUrl` with no text)

See each platform's schema for media constraints.

## LinkedIn @mentions

Mention a person or company by putting its LinkedIn URL inside `@[...]`, in `content`, a LinkedIn entry's `customContent` or its `platformSpecificData.firstComment`. The post is published with LinkedIn's real name and link, with no lookup call first.

- Person: `@[https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe]`
- Company: `@[https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme]`
- Your own text: `@[Jane](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe)`. For a person it must be the first, last or full name, for a company the exact company name, both case-sensitive. Other text is replaced with LinkedIn's name and returns a `linkedin_mention_name_replaced` warning.
- `@[Text](urn:li:person:ID)`, as returned by `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/linkedin-mentions`: published exactly as written, with no lookup, so its text must already be LinkedIn's name.

A post can resolve at most 10 profile or company URL mentions across its shared content, LinkedIn entries and first comments. Resolving a person's profile URL needs one of your LinkedIn accounts to administer a Page; publishing does not.

### When a mention can't be resolved

Only profile and company URLs can fail. A scheduled or published post is rejected with:

- `400` `linkedin_mentions_invalid`: a URL could not be resolved
- `400` `linkedin_mentions_limit_exceeded`: more than 10 URL mentions
- `401` `reconnect_required`: the LinkedIn token expired
- `429` `rate_limited`: LinkedIn is rate limiting
- `503` `temporarily_unavailable` (retryable): LinkedIn did not answer within 8 seconds in total

`details.mentions[]` (`LinkedInMentionIssue`) lists each failing mention with its own code:

- `linkedin_mention_unresolvable`
- `linkedin_mention_requires_page_admin`
- `linkedin_mention_name_unavailable`: LinkedIn withheld the name and none was given

Drafts never fail on a mention: unresolved ones (and more than 10) stay as written and come back as `warnings`. A draft is checked again when it is scheduled.

### On other platforms

`@[linkedin.com/in/jane]` is posted as its text, or as the vanity (`jane`) when you wrote no text, and `@[Text](urn:li:...)` as `Text`.

## Scheduling

Pick one of:

- `scheduledFor`: publish at the scheduled time
- `publishNow: true`: publish synchronously, inside this request
- `queuedFromProfile`: publish in the profile's next queue slot

With none of them and `isDraft` unset, the post is saved as a draft. `platforms` is required unless the post is a draft.

Precedence:

- `isDraft: true` wins over `publishNow` and `scheduledFor` (the post is saved, never published).
- `publishNow: true` wins over `scheduledFor`.
- A `scheduledFor` already in the past is not rejected: the post is published synchronously in the same request, exactly like `publishNow`.

## Idempotency

Three layers of duplicate-protection apply, so safe-to-retry callers (network blips, n8n / Zapier retries, etc.) don't accidentally double-post. They are checked in this order:

1. An `Idempotency-Key` match (200)
2. Same-`x-request-id` retries (200)
3. The content-hash dedup (409)

### 1. `Idempotency-Key` (recommended for retries, 24-hour window)

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (a UUID per logical post, up to 255 characters). Reuse it when you retry after a 5xx, a timeout or a dropped connection.

A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns **HTTP 200** with the original post in the `post` field, and no new post is created.

The match is on the key alone, not on the body: a retry returns the original post even if its body differs (for example a re-uploaded media URL).

It covers drafts, and a post that was saved even though the original response was a 5xx or timed out.

- If the first request is still being processed, the retry gets **HTTP 409** with `code: idempotency_conflict` and a `Retry-After` header; retry after that delay.
- If the first request failed without creating a post, the retry is processed as a new request.

Keys are scoped to your user. Never reuse a key for a different post: that post would not be created, and the earlier one would be returned instead.

### 2. `x-request-id` retry detection (24-hour window)

A request may carry the same `x-request-id` as an earlier one AND collide with it on the content fingerprint below (same account, content and media URLs).

Then we return **HTTP 200** with the original post in the `post` field (or **HTTP 202** with `postId` if the original is still being saved) instead of a 409.

A request with the same `x-request-id` but different content is a new post. When both headers are sent, `Idempotency-Key` wins and `x-request-id` is ignored for matching.

The official Zernio SDKs auto-generate a unique `x-request-id` per call. On a generic HTTP client (curl, n8n's HTTP node, Zapier, custom code), either:

- Set a unique `x-request-id` per logical call (UUIDv4 is fine)
- Or omit the header, and we'll treat each request as new

### 3. Content-hash dedup (24-hour window)

Independently, we hash `(platform, accountId, content + media URLs)` and reject duplicates within 24 hours with **HTTP 409**. This catches genuine "same content posted twice to the same account" cases regardless of `x-request-id`.

The response carries `error`, `accountId`, `platform`, and `existingPostId` so you can find the original.

To intentionally re-post identical content within 24h, change something (the caption, the media, the account), because the dedup is keyed on the full content fingerprint.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Optional client-generated key (a UUID per logical post) that makes retries safe. Reuse it on every retry of the same post, especially after a 5xx or a timeout.

- A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the original post (HTTP 200), whatever its body.
- While the original is still processing, it returns 409 `idempotency_conflict` with `Retry-After`.
- Longer than 255 characters returns 400.

Takes precedence over `x-request-id`. See the operation description for the full contract.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description:
Optional client-generated request identifier. SDKs set it automatically.

A request with the same value as an earlier one within 24 hours that also matches its content fingerprint (same account, content and media URLs) returns the original post (HTTP 200) instead of a duplicate-content 409.

It does not protect a retry whose body differs; use `Idempotency-Key` for that. See the operation description for the full idempotency contract.

title.description: Stored on the post for reference/display only. This field is NOT used as the video title when publishing. To set a YouTube video title, use platformSpecificData.title on the youtube platform target (falls back to the first line of content when omitted).

content.description: Post caption/text. Optional when media is attached, all platforms have customContent, every platform entry is an X Article (platformSpecificData.article), or every platform entry is a LinkedIn text-free reshare (platformSpecificData.reshareUrl with no text). Required for other text-only posts. LinkedIn @mentions: write @[https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe] or @[https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme] in the text (see the operation description).

mediaItems.description:
Media attached to every platform in the request (a platform entry can override it with `customMedia`).

- Each entry needs a publicly reachable HTTPS `url`.
- `type` (image, video, gif, document) is inferred from the URL extension when omitted; a `type` that contradicts the extension is rejected with 400.
- Upload files with `POST /v1/media/presign` first.
- Per-platform size, duration and format limits are listed on each platform schema.

platforms.description: Target platforms and accounts for this post. Required for non-draft posts (returns 400 if empty). Drafts can omit platforms.

customContent.description: Platform-specific text override. When set, this content is used instead of the top-level post content for this platform. Useful for tailoring captions per platform (e.g. keeping tweets under 280 characters).

scheduledFor.description: Optional per-platform scheduled time override. When omitted, the top-level scheduledFor is used.

When to publish. Required unless `publishNow` is true, `queuedFromProfile` is set, or the post is a draft. Ignored when `publishNow` is true.

An ISO 8601 value:

- With a `Z` or offset (`2026-01-15T10:00:00Z`, `2026-01-15T11:00:00+01:00`): taken as-is.
- Without one (`2026-01-15T10:00:00` or `2026-01-15 10:00`): read as local time in `timezone`.

A value already in the past is published synchronously in the same request.

publishNow.description: Publish to every platform synchronously in this request instead of scheduling; the response then carries each platform result and `platformPostUrl`, with HTTP 207 when some platforms failed. Takes precedence over `scheduledFor`; ignored when `isDraft` is true.

isDraft.description: When true, saves the post as a draft. When none of scheduledFor, publishNow, or queuedFromProfile are provided, the post defaults to draft automatically.

requiresApproval.description: When true, saves the post as pending_approval instead of scheduled. Needs scheduledFor, at the root or on every platform; cannot be combined with isDraft, publishNow, queuedFromProfile or queueId. The post publishes only after POST /v1/posts/{postId}/review approves it; approving after the scheduled time publishes within a couple of minutes.

dryRun.description:
TikTok only. Preview whether each `tiktok` entry in `platforms` could publish right now under the TikTok Direct Post daily limits, without creating, scheduling or publishing anything.

No post is persisted and no upload slot is claimed, so it can be repeated freely. The request still goes through auth, the payment gate, body validation and the same account access checks as a real create (it can return 400 or 403).

Returns HTTP 200 with `{ dryRun: true, canPublish, tiktok: [...] }` instead of 201. Only `tiktok` entries are evaluated; other platforms are ignored. A body with no `tiktok` entry is rejected with 400 `invalid_field_value` on `platforms`.

Always `canPublish: true` (not subject to the limit):

- Entries with `platformSpecificData.tiktokSettings.draft: true` (Creator Inbox upload).
- Accounts connected through the TikTok for Business app. On those, a dry run confirms the request is well-formed rather than gating it.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone (`Europe/Madrid`, `America/New_York`) used to interpret a `scheduledFor` (root or per-platform) that carries no `Z` or offset. Stored on the post. No effect on values that already carry one.

**When omitted:** the post takes its profile's `timezone` (the queue's profile for a queued post, else the profile its accounts share). UTC when there is none, or the accounts sit on profiles with different timezones.

An unknown name returns 400 when `scheduledFor` is set.

tags.description: Tags/keywords. YouTube constraints: each tag max 100 chars, combined max 500 chars, duplicates auto-removed.

hashtags.description: Stored for reference only. Hashtags are NOT automatically appended to the caption when publishing. Include hashtags directly in the content field (platforms like Instagram only support hashtags as caption text). For YouTube keywords, use the tags field instead.

mentions.description: Stored for reference only. This field does NOT automatically create @mentions when publishing. For LinkedIn @mentions, write them in the post content, for example @[https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe] or @[https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme].

crosspostingEnabled.description: Stored on the post and echoed back on reads. Publishing does not branch on it: every entry in `platforms` is published regardless, so treat it as a label for your own tooling.

metadata.description: Free-form key/value pairs of your own, stored on the post and returned on reads and in webhook payloads. Zernio also writes the bookkeeping keys `usageCounted`, `usageRefunded` and `hidden` into this object; do not set them, and they are stripped from webhook payloads.

tiktokSettings.description: Root-level TikTok settings applied to the TikTok platforms sent in the same request. Merged into each platform's platformSpecificData, with platform-specific settings taking precedence.

facebookSettings.description: Root-level Facebook settings applied to the Facebook platforms sent in the same request. Merged into each platform's platformSpecificData.facebookSettings, with platform-specific settings taking precedence.

queuedFromProfile.description: Profile ID to schedule via queue. When provided without scheduledFor, the post is auto-assigned to the next available slot. Do not call /v1/queue/next-slot and use that time in scheduledFor, as that bypasses queue locking.

queueId.description:
Specific queue ID to use when scheduling via queue.
Only used when queuedFromProfile is also provided.
If omitted, uses the profile's default queue.

twitterArticle.description:
Creates an X Article draft and publishes it. This normally makes two
billable X API calls at $0.010 each ($0.020 total). The account must
be eligible for X Articles (X Premium+). Article media is supplied as
public URLs; Zernio uploads it to X and builds the native media shape.

blocks.text: Long-form publishing should be observable. Read the implementation notes.

twitterArticleDraft.summary: Save an X Article as a platform draft
twitterArticleDraft.description: Creates only the X Article draft ($0.010) and does not publish it publicly.

blocks.text: This Article is ready for final review.

facebookDraft.summary: Facebook draft post (visible in Publishing Tools)

value.content: Draft post for review before publishing

facebookCarousel.description:
Posts a 2-10 card carousel where each image has its own click-through link
and optional headline. mediaItems and carouselCards must have the same
length, in the same order. Images only (no video cards).

facebookTextBackground.description:
Renders the post as large text on a Facebook-defined colored background.
Text-only: mediaItems and carouselCards are rejected, and contentType
must not be story or reel.

recyclingPost.summary: Post with weekly recycling and content variations

tiktokPhotoCarousel.description:
Sends photos to TikTok Creator Inbox as a draft. The creator receives an inbox
notification and completes the post via TikTok's editing flow. Uses draft: true
which maps to TikTok API post_mode MEDIA_UPLOAD. Note: publish_type is not a
supported field; use draft instead.

tiktokPhotoDirect.description:
Publishes photos directly to TikTok. With draft omitted or false, the post is
published immediately via TikTok API post_mode DIRECT_POST.

tiktokVideoDraft.description:
Sends a video to TikTok Creator Inbox as a draft. Video drafts use a dedicated
TikTok endpoint (/v2/post/publish/inbox/video/init/) that only accepts source_info,
so post_info fields (privacyLevel, allowComment, etc.) are set by the creator
during TikTok's editing flow.

value.content: We just launched our new product!

200.description:
Nothing was created. Either a dryRun preview (TikTok only), which deliberately carries no
numeric cap detail, only a per-account go/no-go and a reason; or a retry matched by
`Idempotency-Key` or `x-request-id`, which returns the original post
(`PostCreateResponse`, with `message: "Post already exists (idempotent retry)"`).

A newly created post is always a 201.

scheduled.summary: Scheduled post (URLs populated after publish time)

207.description:
The post was created, but the inline publish (`publishNow: true`, or a `scheduledFor` that is already due) did not fully succeed.

**207 is a 2xx status.** `fetch(...).ok` is `true` and axios' default `validateStatus` resolves, so a client that only checks for success reads this as a published post. Branch on the status code explicitly.

Tell the outcomes apart with `post.status`:

- `partial`: at least one platform published and at least one failed. Per-platform detail is in `platformResults` and `post.platforms[]`.
- `failed`: no platform published. Terminal; nothing will be retried. Read `platforms[].errorMessage`, `platforms[].errorCategory` and `platforms[].errorSource` to decide whether the caller, the platform or Zernio must act.
- `scheduled`: every platform hit a transient error and was reset to `pending`. Zernio retries automatically. This is **not** a failure; do not surface it to an end user as one.

A publish attempt that aborted before it started (for example the post was already being processed) reports none of the three: `post.status` is unchanged and `platformResults` is absent. Read `error` and `post.platforms[]`, which is always present.

allPlatformsFailed.summary: Every platform failed (post.status is failed, terminal)

platforms.errorMessage: Facebook needs you to confirm your identity before you can publish as this Page. Open the Facebook mobile app, go to this Page, and complete the identity confirmation, then try again.

platformResults.error: Facebook needs you to confirm your identity before you can publish as this Page. Open the Facebook mobile app, go to this Page, and complete the identity confirmation, then try again.

temporaryErrorsWillRetry.summary: Transient errors (post.status is scheduled, Zernio retries)

value.error: Publishing encountered temporary errors. The post will be retried automatically.

400.description: Validation error. A LinkedIn profile or company URL mention that cannot be resolved returns code `linkedin_mentions_invalid` with `details.mentions[]`.

403.description:
Forbidden. Distinguish by the `code` field:

- `ACCOUNT_DISCONNECTED`: a target account's platform connection is no longer active (token expired or revoked, or disconnected). Reconnect it, then refresh account IDs from `GET /v1/accounts` (connection state is in `isActive`). The disconnect is also emitted as the `account.disconnected` webhook event.
- `ACCOUNT_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_POSTING`: a target account was connected for ads only (`enabled: false`). Connect it as a posting account (it then counts as a connected account), then refresh account IDs from `GET /v1/accounts`.
- `PROFILE_OVER_LIMIT`: a target account belongs to a profile beyond the plan's profile limit.
- No `code`: a target `accountId` does not belong to the authenticated user (or is outside the API key's profile scope).

error.example: Account exemple-id (facebook "My Page") is disconnected and cannot be posted to. Facebook tokens expired. Please reconnect your Facebook account. After reconnecting, refresh your account IDs from GET /v1/accounts.

code.description: Stable machine-readable cause. Absent for ownership failures.

409.description:
Duplicate content detected. Returned when the requested post matches an existing one on `(platform, accountId, content-hash)` within the last 24 hours, AND the request was NOT an `x-request-id` retry. Distinct from same-`x-request-id` retries (which return HTTP 200 with the original post; see operation description for the idempotency contract).

Also returned with `code: idempotency_conflict` and a `Retry-After` header when a request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed. Retry after the delay to get the original post.

Body fields:
- `error`: human-readable message
- `details.accountId`: the account that already has this content
- `details.platform`: the platform that already has this content
- `details.existingPostId`: Zernio `_id` of the original post

To intentionally re-post identical content within 24h, vary the content fingerprint (change the caption, swap a media item, or use a different account). To avoid 409s caused by retry loops, set a unique `x-request-id` per logical request. See `parameters.x-request-id` above.

error.example: This exact content is already scheduled, publishing, or was posted to this account within the last 24 hours.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Possible causes: API rate limit, velocity limit (25 posts/hour per account), account cooldown, or daily platform limits, or LinkedIn rate limiting a LinkedIn mention lookup (code `rate_limited`).

details.description: Additional context about the rate limit

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate limit resets (for API rate limits)

get.description: Returns a paginated list of posts. Published posts include platformPostUrl with the public URL on each platform. A query parameter that is not listed here returns 400 naming it and the accepted parameters, so a misspelled filter never silently returns the unfiltered list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Values above the maximum return 400 rather than being clamped.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Row offset. Takes precedence over page when both are sent; the response pagination.page is derived from it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque cursor from a previous response's `pagination.nextCursor`. Returns the next page in the same `sortBy` order and takes precedence over `page` and `offset`.

Each cursor page costs the same however deep it is, unlike `page`/`offset`, which get slower the further you go. Prefer it to walk a long history.

- Send the same filters and `sortBy` as the request that issued it. A cursor from another `sortBy` returns 400.
- Not available with `sortBy=status` or `sortBy=platform`, or with `source=external`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of post fields to return. Each post then carries `_id` plus only these fields, which makes large pages much cheaper: leave out `platforms`, `content`, `mediaItems` or `metadata` when you do not need them.

Accepted: `userId`, `title`, `content`, `mediaItems`, `platforms`, `scheduledFor`, `timezone`, `status`, `tags`, `hashtags`, `mentions`, `visibility`, `metadata`, `recycling`, `recycledFromPostId`, `queuedFromProfile`, `queueId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.

An unknown field returns 400 naming it. `fields=_id` returns ids only. Omit it (or send it empty) for the full post. Not available with `source=external`.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description:
Only posts whose `updatedAt` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (an offset or `Z` required).

`updatedAt` moves when the post or any of its platforms changes (an edit, a status change, a platform publishing or failing). To keep a copy in sync, send the time of your previous sync instead of reading every page again.

Combines with the other filters and with `cursor`. Deleted posts are not returned. Not available with `source=external`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Which collection to read. `zernio` (default) returns posts authored through Zernio. `external` returns posts synced from the platform (existing/historical posts that were published outside Zernio). Combine with `accountId` and paginate via `page`/`limit` to walk the full synced history (we keep up to the last ~12 months per account).

parameters.name: profileId
parameters.description: Filter posts to a specific profile (24-char hex ObjectId). Omit it, or send `all` or an empty value, to list posts across every profile.

parameters.name: createdBy
parameters.description: Filter posts to those created by a specific team user (24-char hex ObjectId).

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD, or a full ISO 8601 datetime. An empty value means no date filter; any other malformed value returns 400. The same name the other date-window filters use (ads, analytics).

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description: Zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD, or a full ISO 8601 datetime. An empty value means no date filter; any other malformed value returns 400. The same name the other date-window filters use (ads, analytics).

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Alias of fromDate, kept for existing callers

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Alias of toDate, kept for existing callers

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search posts by text content.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated tags (at most 20). Returns only posts carrying every listed tag, matched exactly and case-sensitively against the tags set when the post was created. An empty value means no tag filter. `tag` is accepted as an alias.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Sort order for results.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Filter posts to those published via a specific account (24-char hex ObjectId).

put.description:
Update an existing post. Draft, scheduled, failed, partial, and cancelled posts can be edited. Published posts can only have their recycling config updated.

To promote a draft to scheduled, send `isDraft: false` together with `scheduledFor` (or `publishNow: true`, or `queuedFromProfile`). If `isDraft` is omitted the post keeps its current draft status, so sending only `scheduledFor` to a draft returns 200 but the post remains a draft.

Non-draft updates run the same per-platform validation as post creation (media requirements, platform-specific field rules, etc.) against the resulting platforms, returning 400 on failure.

## LinkedIn @mentions

Profile and company URLs in the `content` or LinkedIn `customContent` you send are resolved to LinkedIn's name and link, exactly as on `POST /v1/posts` (see Create post for the rules). For example:

- `@[https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe]`
- `@[Jane](https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme)`

Only what the request sends is looked up: an update of the schedule, status or media makes no LinkedIn call, and `@[Text](urn:li:...)` markup is stored as written.

Moving a draft out of draft also resolves the stored `content` and the stored `customContent` of its LinkedIn entries, and saves the result.

### When a mention can't be resolved

On a non-draft, the request returns one of these, with each mention under `details.mentions[]` (`LinkedInMentionIssue`):

- `400` `linkedin_mentions_invalid`
- `429` `rate_limited`
- `401` `reconnect_required`
- `503` `temporarily_unavailable` (retryable)

Drafts get `warnings` instead.

title.description: Stored on the post for reference/display only. This field is NOT used as the video title when publishing. To set a YouTube video title, use platformSpecificData.title on the youtube platform target (falls back to the first line of content when omitted).

platforms.description: Target platforms and accounts for this post. Each item must include platform and accountId.

scheduledFor.description: Optional per-platform scheduled time override. It is kept when a top-level scheduledFor is also sent, except a date sent back unchanged (same instant, or the same wall-clock time in the post's previous timezone) that matched the post scheduled time or is already past, which follows the new top-level scheduledFor.

platformSpecificData.description: A <platform>Settings namespace (e.g. facebookSettings, tiktokSettings) omitted from the request is preserved from the stored post. Sending the key replaces the whole namespace; it is not deep-merged.

isDraft.description: When omitted, the post keeps its current draft status. Send `false` to promote a draft to scheduled (combined with `scheduledFor`, `publishNow`, or a queue).

requiresApproval.description: Send true on a draft to submit it for approval: it becomes pending_approval and publishes only after POST /v1/posts/{postId}/review approves it. Cannot be combined with isDraft, publishNow, queuedFromProfile or queueId. Returns 409 when the post is not a draft.

hashtags.description: Stored for reference only. Hashtags are NOT automatically appended to the caption when publishing. Include hashtags directly in the content field (platforms like Instagram only support hashtags as caption text). For YouTube keywords, use the tags field instead.

queuedFromProfile.description: Profile ID to schedule via queue.

queueId.description: Specific queue ID to use when scheduling via queue.

tiktokSettings.description: Root-level TikTok settings applied to the TikTok platforms sent in the same request. Merged into each platform's platformSpecificData, with platform-specific settings taking precedence. Returns 400 if sent without a platforms array.

facebookSettings.description: Root-level Facebook settings applied to the Facebook platforms sent in the same request. Merged into each platform's platformSpecificData.facebookSettings, with platform-specific settings taking precedence. Returns 400 if sent without a platforms array.

207.description:
The post was updated, but the inline publish that followed did not fully succeed.

**207 is a 2xx status**, so `fetch(...).ok` is `true` and axios resolves. Branch on the status code explicitly.

Read `post.status`: `partial` (some platforms published), `failed` (none published, terminal), or `scheduled` (transient errors, platforms reset to `pending`, Zernio retries automatically and this is not a failure). `platformResults` is omitted when the attempt aborted before producing per-platform results; `post.platforms[]` is always present.

400.description: Invalid request. A LinkedIn profile or company URL mention that cannot be resolved returns code `linkedin_mentions_invalid` with `details.mentions[]` (`LinkedInMentionIssue`).

409.description:
Conflict. One of:

- `queue_slot_conflict`: the requested scheduledFor collides with another post already in that slot of the same queue. Choose a different time, omit scheduledFor to let the queue assign the next open slot, or send queueId: null to schedule outside the queue.
- `invalid_resource_state`: requiresApproval was sent on a post that is not a draft.

get.description:
Returns analytics for posts. With postId, returns a single post. Without it, returns a paginated list with overview stats.

- Accepts both Zernio Post IDs and External Post IDs (auto-resolved).
- fromDate defaults to 90 days ago if omitted, max range 366 days.
- Single post lookups may return 202 (sync pending) or 424 (all platforms failed).
- For follower stats, use /v1/accounts/follower-stats.

### LinkedIn personal accounts

Analytics are only available for posts published through Zernio. LinkedIn's API only returns metrics for posts authored by the authenticated user. Organization/company page analytics work for all posts.

### Facebook Page stories

Stories on a connected Page, published through Zernio or natively, are collected while they are live and returned like any other post (platformPostUrl points to the story). Metrics for a story published through Zernio are available on its Zernio post ID.

Their lifetime metrics refresh about hourly, with a final reading shortly before the story expires at 24 hours. After that the values stay at that last reading.

Mapping:

- impressions = story media views (Meta stopped accepting per-story impressions in October 2026, so impressions equals views)
- reach = unique story media viewers
- views = story media views
- likes = story reactions
- comments = story replies
- shares = story shares
- clicks: always 0, because Meta exposes no link-click metric for stories

parameters.description: Returns analytics for a single post. Accepts Zernio Post IDs, External Post IDs and the platform's native post ID. Zernio IDs are auto-resolved to External Post analytics.

parameters.name: platform

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 90 days ago if omitted. Max range is 366 days.

parameters.name: toDate

parameters.name: sortBy

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order

parameters.name: tags

Note: The list endpoint returns External Post IDs. Posts originally
scheduled via Zernio will have isExternal: true in this response.
Use platformPostUrl to correlate with your original Zernio Post IDs.

202.description:
Analytics are being synced from the platform, or (single post lookup only) the post has not finished publishing on every platform yet.

The body matches AnalyticsSinglePostResponse with syncStatus "pending" and a message.

- While a platform has not published, status is the post's own status (for example scheduled or publishing).
- A post with one failed platform returns 202 rather than 424 until the others finish.
- Pending platforms whose account failed its last analytics sync carry that error in platformAnalytics[].errorMessage, and the message says so.

402.description: Analytics access required. Legacy plans need the Analytics add-on; included by default on usage-based plans.

424.description: Post failed to publish on all platforms. Analytics are unavailable. (single post lookup only)

hasAnalyticsAccess.description: Whether user has analytics add-on access

pagination.description: Present on a paginated request: `{ page, limit, total, pages }` with page and limit, `{ limit, nextCursor }` with cursor paging (limit alone or cursor).

profileTotals.description: Only with profileIds and perProfile. Accounts matching the filters per profile ID; a profile with none is absent.

statusCounts.description: Only with includeStatusCounts=true. Counts over every filter of the request except status.

all.description: Accounts matching the filters in any status.

disconnected.description: Of those, the accounts that need reconnection.

platformUserId.description:
The account's id on its platform, as the platform reports it to Zernio. Stable across reconnects, so use it to match an account against your own records.

- **Instagram Login accounts:** the app-scoped user id (the professional account id is in `metadata.instagramScopedId`).
- **Instagram via Facebook Login:** the professional account id (`17841...`).
- **TikTok:** the open_id of Zernio's TikTok app, which differs from the open_id any other app sees for the same user.

Either value can be passed back as `expectedPlatformUserId` on GET /v1/connect/{platform}.

scopeAreas.description: Accounts connected through your own OAuth app: the permission areas the connect requested. Null on accounts connected through Zernio's app.

oauthAppId.description: The id of your own OAuth app this account connected through (see /v1/connect/oauth-apps); null when it uses Zernio's app.

tiktokAccountType.description:
TikTok accounts only. The account type TikTok reported when the account was connected.

- `personal`: cannot use TikTok direct messages through the API (TikTok limits Business Messaging to Business Accounts). Skip the inbox for them and tell the user to switch to a Business Account in the TikTok app, then reconnect.
- `business`: the prerequisite, not a guarantee. Messaging also needs the messaging scopes granted and TikTok's regional availability.
- `unknown`: accounts connected before this was captured, or whose grant left out the account-type scope.

profilePicture.description: URL to the account's profile picture on the platform. May be null if the platform does not provide one.

profileUrl.description: Full profile URL for the connected account on its platform.

needsReconnection.description:
The platform definitively reported the stored OAuth token as dead.
While true, GET /v1/connect/{platform}/ads returns a
fresh authUrl (implicit force=true) instead of alreadyConnected,
so re-running the connect flow recovers the account. Cleared
automatically when the account is re-authorized.

followersCount.description: Follower count (only included if user has analytics add-on)

followersLastUpdated.description: Last time follower count was updated (only included if user has analytics add-on)

parentAccountId.description:
Reference to the parent posting SocialAccount. Set for ads accounts that share
or derive from a posting account's OAuth token. null for standalone ads (Google Ads)
and all posting accounts. Meta ads business-login accounts also have no parent.

enabled.description:
Whether the user explicitly activated this account. false means the account was created as a side effect (e.g., a posting account auto-created when the user connected ads first).

- GET /v1/accounts still returns such accounts unless `excludeHidden=true` is passed.
- They cannot be posted to (`ACCOUNT_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_POSTING`) and are not billed as connected accounts.
- On an ads account (`metaads`, `googleads`, ...) the value does not hide the connection: ads accounts are listed whatever their `enabled` value and keep working for ads.

rateLimitedUntil.description:
End of the account's publishing cooldown. Compare it with the current time: a value in the past means the cooldown has ended (the field is cleared on the next successful publish); null means no cooldown since the last successful publish.

**When it starts.** A post to the account fails with `errorCategory` `user_abuse` (spam, abuse or rate-limit errors), or 10 or more posts to it fail within an hour with `user_content`, `platform_error`, `platform_rate_limit` or `unknown`.

**How long.** It doubles with each start inside a 24-hour window that opens at the first one (10, 20, 40, 80 minutes and so on, capped at 24 hours).

On a YouTube account with a recorded successful upload, it instead runs until 24 hours after that upload, or 1 hour when that upload is older than 24 hours.

**Effect.** While it is in the future, POST /v1/posts (drafts excepted) and POST /v1/posts/{postId}/retry return 429 for this account. When it starts, this account's pending targets on posts scheduled before the cooldown ends are failed.

metadata.description:
Platform-specific metadata. Fields vary by platform.

**WhatsApp accounts:**

- qualityRating: phone number quality rating from Meta (GREEN, YELLOW, RED, or UNKNOWN).
- nameStatus: display name review status (APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW, DECLINED, or NONE). A declined or pending name does not by itself block sending; sendability is reported separately via health_status (can_send_message).
- messagingLimitTier: maximum unique business-initiated conversations per 24h rolling window (TIER_250, TIER_1K, TIER_10K, TIER_100K, or TIER_UNLIMITED). Scales automatically as quality rating improves.
- verifiedName: Meta-verified business display name.
- displayPhoneNumber: formatted phone number (e.g., "+1 555-123-4567").
- wabaId: WhatsApp Business Account ID.
- phoneNumberId: Meta phone number ID.

**Meta ads business-login accounts:**

- tokenType: system-user.
- businessId: the owning Business Manager ID when there is one owner; null for multiple owners.
- businessIds: owning Business Manager IDs discovered from granted ad accounts.
- grantedAdAccountIds: ad-account IDs granted to the token.
- adAccountBusinesses: map from ad-account ID to its owning business ID or null.
- availablePages: granted Page IDs and names. No Page tokens are exposed.
- selectedPageId: the Page selected for creatives and lead forms, or null.
- scopedAdAccountIds: existing sync scope preserved on reconnect.

Non-expiring tokens have no tokenExpiresAt field. Parent posting reconnects do not replace this token.

**LinkedIn accounts:** profileData carries profile details refreshed on each daily snapshot.

- profileData.bio: the member's headline (personal accounts) or the organization description (organization accounts). null when not set.
- profileData.extraData.vanityName: the member's profile slug, the /in/{vanityName} segment of profileUrl. Personal accounts only; an organization's slug is in metadata.organizationInfo.vanityName.

**Instagram accounts:**

- loginMethod: "facebook_login" when connected through Facebook Login; absent for Instagram Login. On facebook_login accounts, comment reads leave hidden comments out entirely instead of returning them with isHidden true.
- instagramScopedId: the Instagram professional account id (`17841...`). On Instagram Login accounts it is the same whichever app connected the account, while platformUserId is app-scoped. Facebook Login accounts hold this id as platformUserId.

**X (Twitter) accounts:**

- profileData.extraData.isPremium: whether X reports a paid subscription (Basic, Premium, Premium+, or a blue verified badge), which raises the post length limit from 280 to 25,000 characters. Read live at connect and reconnect, refreshed by the daily follower snapshot.
- Because X intermittently reports no subscription for subscribed accounts, a cancellation is stored on the fourth consecutive daily snapshot reporting it (about four days). Accounts connected before the extraData layout carry the flag at profileData.isPremium.

timezone.description: IANA timezone new posts on this profile use when the request names no `timezone`. Null means UTC.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for this profile, set on create or update. Null when none is set.

isOverLimit.description: Only present when includeOverLimit=true. Indicates if this profile exceeds the plan limit.

accountCount.description: In the profile list. Connected accounts on the profile, including ones that need reconnecting; phone and SMS number internals and posting accounts hidden by an ads connect are not counted.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; pass it back as `cursor`. Null on the last page.

ErrorResponse.description:
Canonical error envelope. `error` is the human-readable message; `type`,
`code`, `param`, `platform`, and `platformError` are top-level siblings
for programmatic handling. For upstream platform failures (`type:
platform_error`), `platformError` carries the provider's raw payload
verbatim (for Meta: `error_subcode`, `error_user_title`, `error_user_msg`).

param.description: The request field that caused the error, when applicable.

docUrl.description: Documentation page for resolving the error, when one applies.

platform.description: Upstream platform (e.g. meta, google, tiktok), present when type is platform_error.

platformError.description:
Raw error payload from the upstream platform, passed through verbatim so
integrators can read provider-specific codes. For Meta this includes
error_subcode, error_user_title, and error_user_msg.

details.description:
Additional structured context for the error (for example field-level validation errors). What it carries depends on the endpoint and platform.

**Meta ads refusals.** The ones customers hit most come back with their own `code` instead of `platform_api_error`, the field to fix in `param`, and `details.fix` ({ label, url }) pointing at the Meta page that resolves it:

- `ad_account_payment_required`
- `ad_account_policy_not_accepted`
- `meta_security_check_required`
- `meta_action_blocked`
- `whatsapp_number_not_linked`
- `invalid_targeting`

Meta's own error stays in the message and in `platformError`.

**Private replies.** `privateReplyConsumed` appears on the private-reply endpoint's 400 when the comment's single reply is already spent. `privateReplyOutcome: "unknown"` appears on its 502 when Meta answered a server error and the reply may have been delivered.

**Google quota 429.** On a Google Ads or YouTube Analytics 429, `quotaExhausted: true` marks the failure as Google's own quota, not a Zernio rate limit, so you can keep calling other platforms instead of backing off everywhere. When Google names the scope, `quotaScope` is also set:

- `DEVELOPER`: the shared budget (the developer token for Google Ads, the Google Cloud project for YouTube Analytics). Every account on Zernio is affected and there is nothing to change on your side.
- `ACCOUNT`: your own ad account (Google Ads only).

A Meta 429 carries neither field.

**Zernio Google Ads burst-limit 429.** Carries `budgetScope` instead, never `quotaExhausted`. These are Zernio's own limits, applied before the call reaches Google, and both clear within a minute. They are separate axes from `quotaScope`, not the same pool named twice.

- `account`: the limit of 15 requests per minute per connected Google Ads account.
- `user`: the ceiling of 120 requests per minute per Zernio user across all their Google Ads accounts.

**Failed Meta ad create** (`POST /v1/ads/create`, `POST /v1/ads/boost`, `POST /v1/ads/ctwa`). Carries `stage` (where it failed), `adAccountId` (on which ad account) and `createdObjects` (every object this request had already created, with what cleanup did to it).

- `left_behind` objects still exist on the ad account (Meta refused the delete, typically on a held account, or the delete hit a network error). Delete them yourself or reuse them.
- `unconfirmedWrite` is set when Meta answered a create with a 5xx or dropped the connection and Zernio could not confirm whether the object exists. Check that parent before creating it again.

**Ineligible ad account: 422 `ad_account_unusable`.** When Meta refuses a write because the ad account's status is ineligible to manage ads (Meta subcode 2490592 or 4841021, on the write itself or on a cleanup delete), any Meta ads write answers it.

That covers create, boost, CTWA, campaign / ad set / ad updates and status changes.

The message names the ad account when known, links Meta's fix (https://www.facebook.com/business/help/0), lists the objects left behind and ends with Meta's original error, which also stays verbatim in `platformError`.

Meta often reports the first failure under an unrelated code (e.g. 1487194 on the creative), so branch on `code`, not on `platformError`.

**Missing Advertise permission: 403 `insufficient_permissions`.** When the Facebook user behind the connection's token lacks the Advertise permission on the ad account, any Meta ads write answers it.

Triggers: Meta subcode 2490585, 2490591 or 4841020 on the write, or a code 200 refusal such as 1487194 whose cleanup deletes Meta refused with 2490591 or 4841020.

Meta may still accept the campaign and ad set and refuse only the ad. The message names the ad account, asks for the Advertise or Manage permission on it (or a token granted `ads_management`, by reconnecting) and lists the objects left behind.

It ends with Meta's `error_user_title`, `error_user_msg` and subcode; the raw error stays in `platformError`.

stage.description:
Meta ad create failures only. The step that failed:

- `media`: image/video download or upload.
- `campaign`
- `adset`
- `creative`
- `ad`: the ad POST itself, where Meta's code 31 / 3858385 hold and 100 / 1359188 payment rejections land.
- `activation`: switching the created objects on. No longer returned: a refused switch to ACTIVE now answers 201 with an `activation_failed:` warning and the objects kept PAUSED.
- `other`: a read or check before any write.

adAccountId.description: Meta ad create failures only. The ad account the request wrote to (`act_...`).

createdObjects.description: Meta ad create failures only. Every object this request created before failing, in creation order. Objects you referenced (an existing campaign, ad set, creative or video) are never listed and never deleted.

id.description: Meta object id; for `image` the image hash.

cleanup.description: `deleted`: Zernio deleted it. `left_behind`: cleanup could not delete it (Meta refused the delete, or the delete hit a network error), so it still exists. `kept`: deliberately not deleted (image hashes are shared by every upload of the same file).

unconfirmedWrite.description: Meta ad create failures only, when Meta answered a create with a 5xx or dropped the connection and the object could not be looked up. Zernio did not retry it.

parentId.description: Where to look for it: the ad set for an ad, the campaign for an ad set, the ad account otherwise.

quotaExhausted.description: Google Ads and YouTube Analytics 429 only. True when the upstream Google quota is spent rather than a Zernio limit.

quotaScope.description: Google Ads and YouTube Analytics 429 only, when the scope is known. DEVELOPER is the shared budget (the developer token for Google Ads, the Google Cloud project for YouTube Analytics); ACCOUNT is your ad account (Google Ads only).

budgetScope.description: Zernio Google Ads burst-limit 429 only (never set alongside `quotaExhausted`). `account` is the limit of 15 requests per minute per connected Google Ads account; `user` is the ceiling of 120 requests per minute per Zernio user across all their Google Ads accounts. Both clear within a minute.

MediaContentType.description: MIME type of the file to upload. Rejected with a 400 (INVALID_FIELD_VALUE on contentType) when it is not one of these values, so generic types such as application/octet-stream are not accepted here.

MediaItem.description: Media referenced in posts. URLs must be publicly reachable over HTTPS. Use POST /v1/media/presign for uploads up to 5GB. Zernio auto-compresses images and videos that exceed platform limits (videos over 200 MB may not be compressed).

type.description: Optional when the item names a connected file (`fileId`): inferred from the file's MIME type.

url.description: A media item with a null, missing or empty url is dropped, unless it names a connected file with `fileId` + `accountId`.

fileId.description:
A file of a connected Google Drive or OneDrive account (see the Files endpoints). Requires `accountId`.

The file is copied into Zernio media storage when the post is created, and the item is stored as a plain `url`. A folder, an undownloadable file or an unknown id fails the request with a 4xx naming `mediaItems[i].fileId`.

accountId.description: The connected Google or Microsoft account the `fileId` belongs to (must have the `files` area). Required with `fileId`.

title.description: Optional title for the media item. Used as the document title for LinkedIn PDF/carousel posts. If omitted, falls back to the post title, then the filename.

altText.description:
Accessibility alternative text for an image. Set once per image; the same value is sent to each selected platform.

- Applied on: Instagram (feed images only, not Reels/Stories), Facebook, Threads, X (max 1000 chars), LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest (max 500 chars).
- Ignored on platforms without alt-text support (TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, Telegram, Reddit, Google Business Profile, WhatsApp) and on video items where the platform does not accept it.

thumbnail.description: Optional custom thumbnail/cover image URL for videos. Supported for Facebook video posts, Facebook Reels, regular video uploads, and LinkedIn video posts. Max 10MB, JPG/PNG recommended.

instagramThumbnail.description: Custom cover image URL for Instagram Reels. Can also be set via platformSpecificData.instagramThumbnail or platformSpecificData.reelCover. Resolution order: this field > platformSpecificData.instagramThumbnail > platformSpecificData.reelCover > platformSpecificData.thumbnailUrl (legacy).

subtitles.description:
Subtitle (closed caption) files for a video item, in SRT or WebVTT. Each language may appear once per video. Zernio downloads each file when the post is created or updated and converts it to the format each platform requires.

Sent to YouTube, Facebook videos, LinkedIn, X and Bluesky; ignored with a warning elsewhere. Per platform:

- YouTube: every track.
- Facebook: every track, up to 200 KB each.
- Bluesky: every track, up to 20 KB each after conversion to WebVTT.
- X: the first track only (one subtitle per video).
- LinkedIn: the first English track only.

Tracks a platform cannot take are skipped and reported in the response warnings.

A file that is unreachable, redirects, exceeds 1 MB, is not valid SRT or WebVTT, or is over a platform limit is rejected with a 400 (code INVALID_SUBTITLES). If a platform rejects a file at publish time, the post still publishes, without subtitles.

tiktokProcessed.description: Internal flag indicating the image was resized for TikTok

url.description: Public http(s) URL of an SRT or WebVTT file: your own host, or an upload from POST /v1/media/presign (contentType application/x-subrip or text/vtt). It must serve the file directly, since redirects are refused.

language.description: BCP-47 language code with a two-letter language, e.g. en, es or pt-BR. Viewers see the track labelled with the language name, e.g. English.

replyToTweetId.description:
ID of an existing tweet to reply to. The published tweet appears as a reply in that tweet's thread. For threads, only the first tweet replies to the target; subsequent tweets chain normally.

X only permits replying to your own posts or posts you are mentioned in; replying to an arbitrary other account's post is rejected by X.

quoteTweetId.description:
ID (or full status URL) of an existing tweet to quote-repost. The published tweet becomes a quote tweet of the target. For threads, applies to the first tweet only.

- Mutually exclusive with media and poll.
- X only permits quoting your own posts, or posts you are mentioned in or part of the conversation thread of. Quoting an arbitrary other account's post is rejected by X.
- Billed at the standard create rate ($0.015), unlike pasting a tweet URL into the text, which is billed at the URL rate ($0.20).

replySettings.description: Controls who can reply to the tweet. "following" allows only people you follow, "mentionedUsers" allows only mentioned users, "subscribers" allows only subscribers, "verified" allows only verified users. Omit for default (everyone can reply). For threads, applies to the first tweet only. Cannot be combined with replyToTweetId.

threadItems.description: Complete sequence of tweets in a thread. The first item becomes the root tweet, subsequent items are chained as replies. When threadItems is provided, the top-level content field is used only for display and search purposes, it is NOT published. You must include your first tweet as threadItems[0].

poll.description: Create a poll with this tweet. Mutually exclusive with media attachments and threads.

options.description: Poll options (2-4 choices, max 25 characters each)

duration_minutes.description: Poll duration in minutes (5 min to 7 days)

longVideo.description:
Uploads the video with X's amplify_video media category instead of the standard tweet_video. Applied only when the connected X account has a paid X subscription; on other accounts the flag is accepted and ignored.

It is not required to post long videos. The standard tweet_video path already publishes videos well past 140 seconds on free accounts, and maximum duration is set by X per account, not by Zernio. Zernio enforces only the 512 MB file-size limit.

Some accounts additionally require X's long-video API allowlisting, without which X rejects an amplify_video upload.

paidPartnership.description: When true, the post is labeled by X as a paid partnership / paid promotion. For threads, applies to the root tweet only. Field availability may depend on your X API access tier.

madeWithAi.description: When true, the post is labeled by X as containing AI-generated media. Per X, this label is for AI-generated media, not AI-written text. For threads, applies to the root tweet only.

sensitiveMedia.description: Marks attached media with a sensitive-content warning. Applied to every media item in the post (requires media; ignored for text-only tweets). At least one flag must be true for the warning to be sent.

mediaTaggedUsers.description: X usernames (with or without @) to tag on the photos of the post, up to 10. Photos only, not video or GIF. Applied to the media of every tweet in a thread. An unknown username fails the post.

TwitterPlatformData.description: X-specific post options. The article field creates a long-form X Article and is mutually exclusive with tweet media and tweet-only options. Geo-restriction applies at the media level: media is hidden outside the specified countries while tweet text remains visible.

mode.description: Publish creates an X Article draft and then publishes it. Draft stops after draft creation and returns the X draft ID without a public URL.

url.description: Public JPG, JPEG, PNG, or WebP URL. GIF, MP4, AVIF, extensionless URLs, and caller-supplied native media IDs are rejected.

XArticle.description:
Long-form X Article payload. Requires an eligible X Premium+ account.

Mutually exclusive with top-level/custom tweet media and with threadItems, poll, quoteTweetId, replyToTweetId, inReplyToTweetId, replySettings, sensitiveMedia, paidPartnership, and madeWithAi.

Publishing normally performs two billable X API requests at $0.010 each (draft + publish, $0.020 total). Mode `draft` performs only the $0.010 draft request.

`articleDraftId` is an internal recovery checkpoint and must not be supplied by API clients.

externalDocs.description: Official X Article content format reference

XArticleContentState.description: X's snake_case content-state shape. Standard DraftJS camelCase fields such as entityMap, inlineStyleRanges, and entityRanges are rejected.

from_index.description: Inclusive start index in the block text.

to_index.description: Exclusive end index in the block text. Must be greater than or equal to from_index and no greater than the block text length.

text.description: Text represented by this metadata range.

XArticleInlineStyleRange.description: The offset plus length must not exceed the containing block's text length.

XArticleEntityRange.description: The referenced entity must exist, and offset plus length must not exceed the containing block's text length.

url.description: Public image, GIF, or MP4 URL. Zernio uploads it to X and replaces it with native media metadata. Caller-supplied media IDs are rejected.

altText.description: Supported for image and GIF URLs; rejected for MP4 media.

XArticleEntity.description: Entity keys must be unique decimal strings matching their zero-based array index (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...).

GeoRestriction.description: Country-level geo-restriction (allowlist). When set, the post is only visible to users in the specified countries. Supported on Facebook (feed posts, videos, reels), X (media-level restriction), and LinkedIn (organization pages only, min 300 targeted followers). Ignored on unsupported platforms. Stories (Facebook, Instagram) do not support geo-restriction.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (uppercase). Only users in these countries can see the post. Maximum 25 countries per post. Example: ["US", "CA", "GB", "ES"].

topic_tag.description: Topic tag for post categorization and discoverability on Threads. Must be 1-50 characters, cannot contain periods (.) or ampersands (&). Overrides auto-extraction from content hashtags when provided.

firstComment.description:
Optional first comment, posted right after publishing as a reply to the published post. With threadItems, it replies to the root post.

Up to 500 characters (the Threads post limit). The reply is itself a Threads post, so it uses one of the 250 posts a profile may publish per 24 hours.

threadItems.description: Complete sequence of posts in a Threads thread. The first item becomes the root post, subsequent items are chained as replies. When threadItems is provided, the top-level content field is used only for display and search purposes, it is NOT published. You must include your first post as threadItems[0].

ThreadsPlatformData.description: Up to 10 images per carousel (no videos). Videos must be H.264/AAC MP4, max 5 min. Images JPEG/PNG, max 8 MB. Use threadItems for reply chains.

contentType.description: Set to 'story' for Page Stories (24h ephemeral) or 'reel' for Reels (short vertical video). Defaults to feed post if omitted.

title.description: Reel title (only for contentType=reel). Separate from the caption/content field.

firstComment.description: Optional first comment to post immediately after publishing (feed posts and reels, not stories). Skipped when facebookSettings.draft is true.

pageId.description: Target Facebook Page ID for multi-page posting. If omitted, uses the default page. Use GET /v1/accounts/{id}/facebook-page to list pages.

FacebookPlatformData.description:
Facebook post settings.

- Feed posts: up to 10 images (no mixed video+image).
- Stories: single media (24h, no captions).
- Reels: a single vertical video (9:16). The Zernio API does not preflight Reel duration; Meta's Reels publishing guide documents 3-90 seconds.
- Geo-restriction: a hard visibility restriction (users outside the specified countries cannot see the post). Not supported for stories.

Draft, carousel and colored-background text options live under facebookSettings, see FacebookSettings.

FacebookSettings.description: Facebook options that must be nested under platformSpecificData.facebookSettings, or sent at the request root as facebookSettings. The remaining Facebook options sit directly on platformSpecificData, see FacebookPlatformData.

draft.description: When true, creates the post as a draft in Facebook Publishing Tools instead of publishing immediately. Supported for feed posts (text, link, image, video) and reels. Not supported for stories. Drafts expire after ~30 days.

carouselCards.description:
Renders the post as a multi-link carousel (organic Page post). Mutually exclusive with contentType=story|reel.

- mediaItems must be provided with the same length, and all items must be images (no videos).
- Each cards[i] adds the click-through link and headline for the image at mediaItems[i].
- Facebook truncates name at ~35 chars and description at ~30 chars on render; longer strings are accepted.

carouselLink.description: Optional top-level "See more" destination shown on the carousel end card. Defaults to the first card's link when omitted. Only used together with carouselCards.

textFormatPresetId.description:
Facebook-defined preset ID that renders the post as large text on a colored background (Graph `text_format_preset_id`). Supply the raw numeric ID from Meta; we do not publish a catalog of presets and Facebook may change the available set.

Pages only (ignored on personal profiles and groups), and text-only feed posts only. Rejected with 400 when mediaItems or carouselCards are present, when contentType is story or reel, or when content is empty. An attachment makes Facebook drop the background silently, so those are rejected up front.

Length is NOT rejected: Facebook's composer stops offering a background at around 130 characters, but Meta documents no API limit, so longer content publishes and returns a warning instead.

A URL detected in the content is NOT attached as a link preview while a preset is set, because a link attachment also makes Facebook drop the background.

contentType.description: Set to 'story' to publish as a Story. Default posts become Reels or feed depending on media.

shareToFeed.description: For Reels only. When true (default), the Reel appears on both the Reels tab and your main profile feed. Set to false to post to the Reels tab only.

collaborators.description: Up to 3 Instagram usernames to invite as collaborators (feed/Reels only)

droppedCollaborators.description: Output only. Set by Zernio when Instagram rejected these collaborators and the retry was sent without them.

reason.description: The reason Instagram gave for rejecting the collaborator

firstComment.description: Optional first comment to add after the post is created (not applied to Stories)

trialParams.description: Trial Reels configuration. Trial reels are shared to non-followers first and can later be graduated to regular reels manually or automatically based on performance. Only applies to Reels.

graduationStrategy.description: MANUAL (graduate from Instagram app) or SS_PERFORMANCE (auto-graduate if performs well with non-followers)

userTags.description:
Tag Instagram users by username. The tag shape depends on the media:

- Photos: require x/y coordinates. Photo tags without valid coordinates are skipped.
- Reels and videos: username only (coordinates are ignored).
- Stories: optional coordinates.
- Carousels: use mediaIndex to target specific slides (defaults to 0); video slides take username-only tags.

username.description: Instagram username (@ symbol is optional and will be removed automatically)

x.description: X coordinate position from left edge (0.0 = left, 0.5 = center, 1.0 = right). Required for photos, ignored for Reels/videos, optional for stories.

y.description: Y coordinate position from top edge (0.0 = top, 0.5 = center, 1.0 = bottom). Required for photos, ignored for Reels/videos, optional for stories.

mediaIndex.description: Zero-based index of the carousel item to tag. Defaults to 0. Tags on out-of-range indices are ignored.

audioName.description: Custom name for original audio in Reels. Replaces the default "Original Audio" label. Can only be set once. Unrelated to audioConfiguration, which attaches a catalog track.

audioConfiguration.description:
Attach a licensed music track or original sound from the Instagram audio catalog to a Reel. Reels only (single video post, not a story or image).

- Requires an Instagram account connected via Facebook Login. Classic Instagram Login accounts get a 400 (instagram_audio_requires_facebook_login).
- Get audio IDs from GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/instagram/audio.
- If the track becomes unavailable by publish time (removed, region-blocked, licensing change), the post fails with a user-error. It is not published without the audio.

audioId.description: Audio asset ID from the audio search endpoint.

audioVolume.description: Volume of the attached audio track, 0-100. Defaults to 100.

videoVolume.description: Volume of the video's own sound, 0-100. Defaults to 100. Set 0 to mute the original video audio.

muteAudio.description:
Publish the video without sound. Applies to Reels, Stories, and video carousel slides; ignored for images.

Instagram has no mute parameter, so we strip the audio track from the file before handing it to Instagram. The published video is permanently silent, and the original audio cannot be restored from Instagram.

- If the audio cannot be stripped, the post fails rather than publishing with sound.
- Videos above 200MB cannot be muted at all, so mute them before uploading.

Unrelated to audioConfiguration.videoVolume, which only lowers the original sound when a catalog track is attached.

thumbOffset.description: Millisecond offset from video start for the Reel cover frame. Ignored when instagramThumbnail or reelCover is provided. Defaults to 0.

instagramThumbnail.description: Custom cover image URL for Instagram Reels (JPG or PNG, publicly accessible). Overrides thumbOffset when provided. Also accepted as reelCover (alias).

reelCover.description: Alias for instagramThumbnail. If both are provided, instagramThumbnail takes priority.

isAiGenerated.description: When true, the post is labeled by Instagram as containing AI-generated media. Per Meta, this self-disclosure label is for AI-generated media, not AI-written captions. Applies to feed posts, Reels, Stories, and carousels.

isPaidPartnership.description: When true, Instagram shows the "Paid partnership" label on the post. Applies to feed posts, Reels, and carousels; not supported on Stories (400). Requires an Instagram account connected via Facebook Login; classic Instagram Login accounts get a 400 (instagram_paid_partnership_requires_facebook_login). Implied when brandedContentSponsors is set.

brandedContentSponsors.description:
Up to 2 brands to tag as sponsors, each an Instagram username (leading @ optional) or a numeric Instagram user ID. Sponsors must be professional (Business or Creator) accounts.

- Usernames are resolved at publish time via the Business Discovery API on the publishing account. A sponsor that cannot be resolved (private, personal, or nonexistent account) fails the post with a user error naming it.
- A brand that has pre-approved the creator shows as "Paid partnership with @brand" immediately; otherwise the plain label shows and the brand receives an approval request.

Sets isPaidPartnership. Same login and content-type rules as isPaidPartnership.

commentsEnabled.description:
When false, comments are turned off on the post right after it is published (Meta's comment_enabled on the media object).

- Applies to feed posts, Reels and carousels; ignored for Stories, which have no comments.
- Works with both Instagram connection methods.
- Best-effort: if the toggle fails after a successful publish, the post still succeeds and stays live with comments on.

locationId.description:
Tags the post with a location: the ID of a Facebook Page that has location data (digits only), sent to Instagram as location_id.

- Applies to feed posts, Reels, and the carousel as a whole.
- Stories and individual carousel slides are unsupported (a Story with locationId is rejected with a 400).
- A Page without location data, or that does not exist, fails the post with a user error at publish time.

InstagramPlatformData.description: Feed aspect ratio 0.5625-1.91, carousels up to 20 items, stories require media (no captions). User tag coordinates 0.0-1.0 from top-left. Images over 8 MB and videos over platform limits are auto-compressed.

documentTitle.description: Title displayed on LinkedIn document (PDF/carousel) posts. Required by LinkedIn for document posts. If omitted, falls back to the media item title, then the filename.

organizationUrn.description: Target LinkedIn Organization URN (e.g. "urn:li:organization:123456789"). If omitted, uses the default org. Use GET /v1/accounts/{id}/linkedin-organizations to list orgs.

firstComment.description: Optional first comment to add after the post is created. Mention with @[https://www.linkedin.com/in/vanity] (resolved to LinkedIn's live name, same rules and errors as post content) or @[Name](urn:li:person|organization:ID); a hand-written name must match LinkedIn's exactly or it renders as plain text.

disableLinkPreview.description: Set to true to disable automatic link previews for URLs in the post content (default is false)

audience.description:
Organization pages only (Zernio rejects it on a personal profile). Audience targeting for the post (Ads Manager's "Targeted audience"), sent as LinkedIn's distribution.targetEntities: OR inside a facet, AND across facets.

LinkedIn rejects the post when the targeted audience is under 300 members.

URN facets accept a full urn:li:<type>:<id> or the bare numeric id. Find ids with GET /v1/ads/targeting/search?platform=linkedin (types country, region, industry, jobFunction, seniority, companySize).

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes with a built-in LinkedIn geo URN (same list as geoRestriction.countries, merged with it). Other countries and sub-country regions go in geoLocations.

geoLocations.description: LinkedIn geo URNs or ids (urn:li:geo:103644278 or 103644278): countries, states, regions, cities.

interfaceLocales.description: Members' LinkedIn interface locale, e.g. { language: es, country: ES }.

staffCountRanges.description: Company size of the member's current employer.

fieldsOfStudy.description: urn:li:fieldOfStudy:<id> or id (LinkedIn standardized fields of study).

organizations.description: Schools, as urn:li:organization:<id> or id (LinkedIn's Organization Lookup).

reshareUrl.description:
LinkedIn post link to repost (use the post's "Copy link to post" action), or a urn:li:share / urn:li:ugcPost / urn:li:groupPost URN. Mutually exclusive with media. Works on personal profiles and organization pages.
